messages.content: I need to log into my account.

function.name: user_authentication_authenticate
function.description: Authenticate a user based on their username and password. Returns a session token if successful. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

username.description: The username of the user attempting to authenticate.

password.description: The password for the user attempting to authenticate.

remember_me.description: Whether to keep the user logged in across sessions.

login_attempts.description: The number of unsuccessful login attempts before this one. If it reaches a certain threshold, additional verification may be required.

message.content: Sure thing! To get you logged in, I’ll need your username and password. If you’d like me to keep you logged in across sessions, just let me know. Once I have those details, I’ll handle the rest.
message.reasoning: The user wants to log into their account. We have a tool function for authentication. We should call the function with the username and password. But we don't have the credentials. We need to ask the user for them. According to policy, we should not request personal data unless necessary. Logging in requires credentials. So we can ask for username and password. We should also ask if they want to remember me. We can ask for login attempts? Probably not needed. So we ask for username and password.
